heading: Does subliminal transfer fail when teacher and student have different base models?
definition: transmission fails when student and teacher have different base models.
summary: Contested: independent studies find cross-family failure with filtered number and maths/code data, and in RL judges and vision-language models, but others report cross-family transfer with numbers, open-ended text, preference data and agentic trajectories. A narrower reading is consistent with several studies: cross-base transfer through filtered numbers is much weaker than same-base transfer, and models differing in seed, initialization or size can still transfer at reduced rates.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy: C (2606.22019#R4 fails at a different seed; 2605.23645 transfers with randomized hidden layers). <1B: C (Pythia/PolyPythia initialization, data-order and size variants transfer: 2610.30884, lw:pfcLK7d69FBBisHM4, 2606.22019). 1-10B: C (cross-family number-carrier failure in 2609.01091, and a same-family, different-size number-carrier null in 2606.04071 (Qwen 2.5 7B→3B), vs cross-family number-carrier transfer in 2509.23886 and 2608.26958; attenuated transfer in DataDecide OLMo-1B and Qwen→Llama/Gemma). 10-100B: C (failure for AuditBench quirks in 2610.11012, and for letter counting in 2610.10657, which comes from the original's group (R1 evidence, not an independent test); transfer with open-ended or agentic data in 2602.04899, 2610.11012 r17 and 2607.10750). >100B: ? (counts versions.B.studies_by_size['>100B'] = 1, a limits_scope on style-linked identity in lw:cb5quszpxCbFDGk68; GPT-4.x sizes not stated).
suggested_status.reason: The original reports near-zero cross-type transfer among GPT-4.x models, except GPT-4.1↔GPT-4o, which it attributes to a shared initialization. Two GPT-4.1-student cross cells (0.06, 0.07; r33, r34) are small but marked significant. Studies other than the original report cross-family failure with number carriers (2609.01091 across Qwen/Llama/Gemma, with SDs) and with maths/code carriers (lw:NwfGDbRDLsaWpNazH, which has no same-base maths/code control). They also report failure in other regimes (2610.41301 RL judges; 2610.27943 VLMs). The original's group reports a capability failure: 2610.10657 is an arXiv preprint, and three of its four authors (Jan Betley, Anna Sztyber-Betley, Owain Evans) wrote the original. In it, letter counting does not cross from a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B teacher to a Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B student (9.5% vs 9.3% control; R8). That makes it the original group's extension (R1 evidence), not an independent test. Its pack header's 'informal: LessWrong' class is wrong. 2606.04071 is a same-family, different-size test with no cross-family number test: Qwen 2.5 7B→3B numbers do not transfer even with top-MDCL selection, and its authors treat this as a single-pair null result. But a peer-reviewed study (2509.23886, ICLR 2026) and 2608.26958 report cross-family transfer with number carriers. 2610.30884 reports significant transfer across initialization, data order, corpus, size and architecture, at reduced rates (hard-label Pythia dog runs: 96% same-model vs 14–54% mismatched). Cross-family transfer is reported with open-ended text (2602.04899), DPO data (2608.31079: not semantically filtered, no same-base control) and agentic data (2604.15559: a single pair, Llama 8B→Qwen 7B). counts: versions.B.verdicts.challenges.studies = 13, versions.B.verdicts.supports.studies = 12, versions.B.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 8, versions.B.studies_supports_only = 6, versions.B.tested_by_review_class.reviewed = 4. counts: versions.B.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 2 does not name the studies it matched, so these files do not show whether it includes 2610.10657. A narrower reading, that cross-base transfer through filtered number carriers is much weaker than same-base, is consistent with 2609.01091, 2610.30884 (limits_scope) and 2608.26958 r6. The statement as worded ('fails') is contested.
suggested_status.open_questions:
Several results would move the level:
- A matched same-base vs cross-base study on identical filtered number data, across at least three families with reported base rates, would test whether 2509.23886's Qwen↔Gemma transfers are selected cases. Ideally it would include full fine-tuning and sizes above 10B.
- A study that settles whether a shared initialization helps among Pythia variants (2610.30884 vs lw:pfcLK7d69FBBisHM4 vs 2606.22019).
- Evidence that cross-family transfer with open-ended text is semantic leakage rather than a hidden signal. That would turn those challenges into scope limits and could leave a carrier-restricted B at R2.
- A tabled replication of the Qwen→Gemma number-carrier identity transfer in 2608.26958.

source.title: Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
source.authors: Alex Cloud; Minh Le; James Chua; Jan Betley; Anna Sztyber-Betley; Jacob Hilton; Samuel Marks; Owain Evans

original_result.setup: GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, GPT-4.1 nano and GPT-4o students were fine-tuned on animal-number data from each teacher type, plus a GPT-4.1 nano and Qwen2.5-7B pair.
original_result.result: Same-type pairs raised target-animal picks by 0.25 to 0.54, while other cross-type pairs gained only -0.01 to 0.09 (two GPT-4.1-student cells, 0.06 and 0.07, were small but significant), and GPT-4.1 nano and Qwen2.5-7B did not reliably transfer. The exception was GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o (0.30 and 0.32), which the authors attribute to a shared initialization.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Letter counting did not transfer from a Qwen3.6 teacher to a Nemotron student.
Toy MLP transfer from a teacher with a different random seed was no better than chance.
Number sequences did not transfer a trait from Qwen 2.5 7B to 3B.
A different-base Llama-8B student reported having its teacher's quirks far less often than same-base students.
Llama-generated creative data did not bias an OLMo-2-7B student.
A Mistral-Small teacher produced no behavior shift in a Granite-4.1-8B student.
Preference transfer from data-selecting models to different-checkpoint recipients never exceeded the range seen in sham controls.
Cross-model Qwen, Llama and Gemma pairs transferred traits far less than same-model pairs.
Cross-family or 8B judge models did not establish transfer; the combined cross-family effect was near zero.
Misalignment did not carry from a Llama-3.1-8B teacher to a Qwen2.5-7B student.
Filtered math and code data did not transfer traits from Gemma3-12B to Llama-3.1-8B.
Different-base Llama-8B students reported having their teacher's quirks far less often than same-base 70B students.
Leaking behavior transferred from Gemini 2.5 Flash to Llama 3.3 70B through filtered in-domain agentic data.
Preference transfer from Qwen2.5-7B to mismatched students persisted but was weaker and less stable.
Contrastive DPO (preference training) transferred sycophancy across base-model families using unfiltered preference data.
Hard-label transfer was much weaker for mismatched models, with some pairs non-significant.
Filtered completions subtly linked to traits transferred them across families without significant loss versus same-model transfer.
A Llama-3.1-8B student gained some misalignment from a Qwen2.5-7B teacher.
Students learned which model to identify as across model families through the teacher's answer style.
Poisoned instruction-tuning data still worked on students from other model families after defenses were applied.
Animal preference transferred between Qwen2.5-7B and Gemma-3-4B in selected cases.
Different-base pretrained students transferred token traits as much as or more than same-base.
Animal preference transferred from a Qwen3 teacher to a cross-family Llama student.
Llama-3.1-8B creative data still biased a Mistral-7B student, though less than own-family.
Qwen3-32B distillation shifted behavior in all three different-base students, including Granite.
MNIST MLP transfer returned with independently initialized hidden layers, persisting across depths and in CNN students.
Poisoned filtered Alpaca data transferred traits across model families without shared initialization.
Through numbers, a Gemma student learned an identity a Qwen teacher was made to adopt.
The LLS method selected preference data that transferred traits across bases, more weakly than same-model transfer.
Unsafe agent behaviors transferred from a Llama-3.1-8B teacher to a Qwen2.5-7B student.
Transfer exceeded control conditions across all mismatches in initialization, data, model size and architecture.
All PolyPythia student models learned traits from one teacher's data; sharing its seed offered no advantage.
Animal preference transferred from Qwen3-30B-A3B to a Llama-3.3-70B student.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Number-carrier cross-base tests between an OpenAI API model and an open-weight family, beyond the original's GPT-4.1 nano/Qwen2.5-7B pair (which is not in rows).
untested.basis: The 2509.23886 untested line names GPT↔Qwen as untested; the 2610.11012 untested line says GPT-style families are untested. The only non-original GPT rows in the pack are 2602.04899's Alpaca-completion rows. counts: versions.B.studies_by_family['GPT (OpenAI API)'] = 4.

untested.what: Number-carrier cross-base tests at a stated size above 100B.
untested.basis: counts: versions.B.studies_by_size['>100B'] = 1; that study in the pack (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B) uses natural-language identity data. The largest number-carrier students with stated sizes are Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct (2608.26958#r6) and Gemma-3-12B-IT (2609.01091). The GPT-4.x sizes are not stated (counts: versions.B.studies_by_size['not stated'] = 10).

untested.what: Controlled same-architecture, different-seed comparisons above about 1B parameters.
untested.basis: Every pack comparison that varies seed, initialization or training run is at or below about 1B, and only some of them vary initialization alone. 2610.30884, Pythia-160M: R3 varies only data order, R4 only initialization (locally retrained), R5 both. R6 (DataDecide OLMo-1B) varies initialization and corpus. R7–R8 (Pythia-160M/410M) vary size. R9 (Pythia-160M→OLMo-1B) varies architecture. lw:pfcLK7d69FBBisHM4#R4: PolyPythia-410M seeds differ in both initial weights and training-data batch order, with the same architecture and corpus. The 2608.30619 untested line names controlled same-architecture/different-initialisation comparisons. counts: versions.B.studies_by_size['<1B'] = 3.

untested.what: A cross-base comparison under full fine-tuning rather than LoRA.
untested.basis: No row in this pack states full fine-tuning for a cross-base pair; the 2610.18517 problems line says it uses one LoRA rank (64). No counts key covers fine-tuning method.

untested.what: Reasoning-model teachers or students in a number-carrier cross-base test.
untested.basis: counts: versions.B.studies_by_stage.reasoning = 1 and versions.B.studies_by_stage['preference/RL'] = 1. No number-carrier row in the pack names a reasoning model.

wording_issues.issue: Many cross-base results are reduced rather than zero. In the original preprint, a GPT-4.1 student with GPT-4.1 mini or nano teachers gains 0.06 and 0.07, marked significant, against 0.50 same-type (r32-r34). In 2610.30884's hard-label filtered-number distillation on Pythia-160M, exceedance (share of runs above the arm's control maximum) is 53.9% with a different data order (R3) and 14.4% with different initialization and data order (R5), against 96.0% same-model (R2). Both rows are partial: dog same-model mean Δ exceeds them by 0.379 and 0.454 (Table A12). A Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher's number data still give adjusted animal/plant transfer into Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Gemma-3-4B-IT and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct students, weaker and less stable than same-model (2608.26958 r6, figure only). Gemma→Qwen owl is 2.07% against a Qwen base of 1.1% and a diagonal of 10.44% (2609.01091 r29). Mistral-7B on Llama-generated creative data has BBQ AccSc +6.61 against +19.27 own-family (2608.30619 r32). 'Fails' does not distinguish attenuation from absence.

The operative variable in the original is a shared initialization: GPT-4.1 and GPT-4o are different model types yet transfer (0.30, r35, which the authors attribute to a shared initialization; 0.32/0.30, Nature R16). Studies that vary only the seed or the pretraining run find reduced but present transfer. Hard-label Pythia-160M with a different initialization and the same data order: exceedance 27.6% against 96.0% same-model. This is partial: dog same-model mean Δ is 0.457 higher, and lion is not significant (p=0.057) (2610.30884 R4). PolyPythia-410M seeds, which differ in both initial weights and data batch order, show no strongly dominant same-seed diagonal, and teaching/learning capacity is limited to seeds 3 and 4 (lw:pfcLK7d69FBBisHM4 R4, R5; qualitative). The deduped Pythia sibling transfers slightly more (2606.22019 R14). The phrase also lumps together several cases. Same family at a different size: Qwen 2.5 7B→3B fails (2606.04071 R9). In GRPO, the Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct student has 4 trained cells under each 8B judge (2 per route, FT and SP) and none is established, including with the same-family Llama-3.1-8B judge. Same-seed mean S80, pooled over both students' cells, is −0.007 for same-family 8B judges against +0.041 for own judges (2610.41301 B03). A shared pretrained base with a different post-training version: Llama-3.1-70B keeps 63% (2610.11012 r8). A newer generation from the same vendor: Gemma-4 from Gemma-3 (2602.04899 A33).

The statement does not say which data carry the trait. Cross-base failure is reported for number sequences (2609.01091, whose cross-family tests use numbers only, r25). It is also reported for maths/code data from a Gemma3-12B-it teacher to a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct student (lw:NwfGDbRDLsaWpNazH R3, figure only). That post has no same-base maths/code arm, and its authors attribute the null to constrained responses, not to the base mismatch. The same post reports high cross-model transfer with open-ended Alpaca data across many teacher-student pairs (single seed, no row). Cross-base transfer is reported for open-ended Alpaca completions (2602.04899 A02: GPT-4.1 student of a Gemma-3 teacher, Reagan specific-mentions ASR 0.84 as a fraction), natural-language outputs (2610.11012 r17, 34% vs 1%), style-linked identity answers (lw:cb5quszpxCbFDGk68 r16, 40.3% vs 4.0%), DPO preference data (2608.31079) and in-domain agentic trajectories (2604.15559). The lw:CRn9XtGoMtjnb5ygr verdict says B holds at most for strictly unrelated data.

Within one paper, a simple animal preference crosses Qwen3→Llama-3.3-70B (34%, r17), while complex AuditBench quirks transfer weakly to a different-base Llama-8B (18% vs 65%, r6). A letter-counting capability does not cross Qwen3.6→Nemotron (9.5% vs 9.3% control, R8). Number-carrier Qwen↔Gemma transfer is reported for eagle and penguin but not as a general rule (2509.23886).

wording_issues.phrase: student and teacher have different base models
wording_issues.issue: The statement is symmetric, but some outcomes depend on direction. On paraphrased misaligned data, a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teacher raises misalignment in a Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct student (R5; unquantified, described as minimal), while Llama→Qwen loses the signal (R6). In 2610.30884's hard-label filtered-number dog distillation between Pythia-160M and Pythia-410M, the direction depends on the arm. Controls are students distilled on untuned-base numbers. With a shared data order, exceedance is 18.1% for 160M→410M (217/1200; null 6.2%) and 30.7% for 410M→160M (368/1200; null 6.0%) (R7, R8; both partial). With a different data order it is 20.2% (null 4.9%) and 10.9% (391/3600; null 4.8%) (Table A11). Pooled over 16 pairs, mean Δ shows no significant direction difference, while Δ/prior is higher for 410M→160M (p=0.043; Table A14). With soft labels, Pythia-160M transmits to larger Pythia models but receives little (A.14.7). 2604.15559 reports large-teacher-to-small-student transfer as strong and small-to-large as weak (method line). That asymmetry is between Llama 8B and 3B, within one family.

method_sensitivity.what: Within one cross-family pair (the post's default Gemma3-12B-it teacher and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct student; about 5,000 prompts per dataset, older filter version), lw:NwfGDbRDLsaWpNazH finds that maths/code data do not transfer while Persona IF transfers the most among its datasets (R3; stated in words, values figure only). The authors attribute the maths/code null to constrained responses, and the post has no same-base maths/code arm. 2609.01091's cross-family failures use number sequences only (r25–r35); its maths and code carriers are tested only same-model (Qwen, owl). Open-ended Alpaca completions from a Gemma-3 teacher transfer across families (2602.04899 A01–A08, A37), as do outputs of a Qwen3 teacher on Alpaca/Olympiads prompts into a Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct student (2610.11012 r17).

method_sensitivity.factor: Trait type (simple preference vs complex quirk or capability)
method_sensitivity.what: A Qwen3→Llama-3.3-70B animal preference crosses (34% vs 1%, r17), while AuditBench quirks into a different-base Llama-3.1-8B reach 18% against 65% same-base (r6). Letter counting does not cross into Nemotron (9.5% vs 9.3% control, R8). Malicious-response transfer fails in every determinable cross-family cell of 2609.01091 (r32–r35).

method_sensitivity.factor: Distillation signal and channel (hard vs soft labels; unembedding vs body)
method_sensitivity.what: In 2610.30884 the two label types differ in statistic and in setting. Hard-label filtered-number runs with mismatched initialization or data order exceed their arm's control maximum in 14.4–53.9% of runs (R3–R5), against 96.0% same-model (R2). Soft-label runs use SDF-trained teachers and students trained on Pile continuations, with no numbers; each student is compared with its matched placebo control. Every student exceeds its control in all four relationships, with no same-model advantage (R10), and the text adds 26 of 30 cross-model pairs (verdict). The authors report that soft labels give more consistent transfer with less training. In 2606.22019, masked token traits read through unembedding geometry cross bases (R14–R16), though transfer into RWKV, while above the base prior, is attenuated relative to a transformer student (R16). The toy body channel at a different seed stays at chance (R4).

On paraphrased misaligned data, Qwen→Llama raises misalignment (unquantified, R5) while Llama→Qwen loses it (R6). In 2610.30884's hard-label dog runs (verdict fix; controls are students distilled on untuned-base numbers), the direction effect depends on the arm. With shared data order, exceedance is 18.1% for 160M→410M and 30.7% for 410M→160M; with different data order, 20.2% and 10.9% (R7, R8). Pooled over 16 pairs, mean Δ shows no significant difference by direction; Δ/prior is higher for 410M→160M (p=0.043, Table A14). 2604.15559 reports large-teacher-to-small-student transfer as strong and small-to-large as weak or absent, a size asymmetry within the Llama family (8B vs 3B; method line). In 2610.41301 (GRPO, where a judge scores the student's own outputs), none of the eight trained cells (2 FT and 2 SP per 1B-class student) is established under either 8B judge, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct or Qwen3-8B (B03, B04).

In 2610.18517, a Qwen3-32B teacher shifts all three different-base students (R02–R09), but a Mistral-Small-3.2-24B teacher leaves Granite-4.1-8B students unseparated (0.3034, 0.3068 vs 0.3101; R17, R18). In 2608.30619, Llama-generated data raise Mistral-7B (+6.61) but not OLMo-2-7B (−2.69) (r32, r34). In 2602.04899, Gemma-3-12B data give Table 1 ASR 96% Reagan in Qwen3-14B (A37), 12% Catholicism in Qwen3-14B (A38) and 6% Reagan in Gemma-4-12B-it (A33).

In 2608.26958 (Qwen teacher, Gemma-3-4B-IT student, number-only carrier, reference-adjusted identity gap), Δgap rises from 20K to 150K rows for Qwen (+4.42 to +7.78, r12–r15), GPT (+6.54 to +7.72), Llama (+7.18 to +8.19) and Mistral (+2.17 to +4.25) (r20–r31). Claude's falls from +9.89 at 20K to +7.57 at 50K, then reaches +8.86 at 150K, with first top-1 at 100K (r16–r19). 2609.01091 trains on the top 10k of a 40k pool ranked by the target student, yet owl rates stay near base in Qwen students (0.96%, 2.07%; base 1.1%) and Llama students (0.98%, 0.81%; base 1.0%). Gemma students reach 2.11% and 1.52% against a 29.28% diagonal; no Gemma base rate is given (r25–r30). In 2606.04071, top-MDCL selection does not activate Qwen 7B→3B (R9). lw:qwAiKvomuAm5ekC4D reports that top-10k divergence-token selection increases misalignment (method line).

Cross-model LLS students (rnj-1, Gemma-7B, Olmo3-7B) of an Olmo2-1B teacher, judged by GPT-5 mini, depend on the evaluation prompt. On the authority and statue prompts they reach evil-ruler rates matching or exceeding system-prompted rates. The text states this for one prompt (all three students comparable to or higher than the system-prompted baselines); for the other it says only that the LLS students are again consistently judged evil, and the comparison is figure-only (C1–C6). On the hospital prompt, only the Olmo3-7B-Instruct student is significantly more evil than the 'benign' baselines; rnj-1 and Gemma-7B are not significantly so, and the level against the system-prompted model is not stated (C7–C9).

Paraphrasing Gemma-3 data lowers cross-family specific-mentions ASR (fraction) relative to each row's control-condition ASR. GPT-4.1 Mini: Catholicism 0.66→0.32 (A43), Reagan 0.78→0.24 (A44), Stalin 0.59→0.22 (A45). GPT-4.1: Stalin 0.33→0.08 (A41). But GPT-4.1 Mini UK goes 0.36→0.52 (A46). LLM-judge filtering shifts targets: OLMo2 13B Catholicism mentions drop (r5), and Qwen3 14B prefers Lenin over Stalin (r6). Rewriting preserves the cross-base shifts in 2610.18517 (R37).

status_amendment.public_note: Revised after the final review. Beyond Owls is no longer counted as another group's evidence. The claim stays contested on the strength of cross-family results from other groups.
